currentContext.expansion: ABDL's capex programme is focused on strengthening backward integration, securing critical inputs (ENA, Malt, PET) and expanding manufacturing capabilities, implemented through Phase I and Phase II investments. Phase I (captive integration): (1) a captive PET bottle manufacturing facility at Rangapur, Telangana was commissioned during the year, with ~600+ Mn bottles per annum capacity and ~70-75% internal requirement coverage, and has been EBITDA accretive since Q3 FY26; (2) a single malt distillery at Rangapur, Telangana (~4.0 MLPA capacity) continued under development to secure captive malt for the Prestige & Above portfolio and build Single Malt whisky capability; (3) an ENA capacity expansion at an acquired ~11 MLPA distillery in Aurangabad, Maharashtra (operations commenced February 2025), with a major expansion initiative underway to significantly increase ENA distillation capacity toward a planned 66 MLPA (also referenced as a planned expansion to ~61 MLPA), strengthening backward integration in a key operating market. Phase II (downstream growth), initiated during the year: bottling capacity expansion in Uttar Pradesh (bottling-unit upgradation, ~40 Cr investment) to strengthen manufacturing presence in a key growth market; bottling capacity expansion at the Aurangabad, Maharashtra facility to support western-market and international demand; and an ENA Distillery (Dual Mode) project in Vizianagaram, Andhra Pradesh via an up-to-50% stake acquired in KION Blenders Industries Private Limited. The narrative text also cites additional investment figures of approximately ~260 Cr, ~110 Cr, ~54 Cr and ~300 Cr associated with the ENA/Phase II projects, but the source formatting does not cleanly attribute each figure to a single named project, so they are reported here only as a range of disclosed amounts rather than assigned individually. Collectively, the current projects are expected to enhance EBITDA margins by ~300 bps by FY28 and an incremental ~100 bps by FY29. ABD Maestro (the super-premium to luxury subsidiary) separately has two strategically located manufacturing facilities in the pipeline to enable efficient small-batch premium production.

risks.risk: Market risk (interest rate, FX, inflation, macro factors)
risks.note: ABDL is exposed to movements in interest rates, foreign exchange rates, inflation and other macroeconomic factors that may influence input costs, pricing, demand and profitability.
Interest rate movements may affect borrowing costs and returns on surplus funds; managed through prudent treasury practices and an appropriate funding mix.
Exposure arises from imports of raw materials, packaging components and capital goods, and from export transactions; currency fluctuations can affect costs and realisations.
Inflation in raw materials, packaging, freight and other operating inputs can pressure margins, requiring cost optimisation, sourcing discipline and calibrated pricing actions.
Arises primarily from trade receivables and placement of surplus funds with banks/financial institutions; managed via credit policies, customer evaluation and expected-credit-loss principles.
Risk of being unable to meet financial obligations as they fall due; managed through cash-flow planning, working-capital review and access to banking lines.

risks.risk: Regulatory and taxation risk (state excise framework)
risks.note: The alcoholic beverages industry operates within a complex and evolving state-level regulatory environment covering excise policy, taxation, licensing and route-to-market structures, which can affect pricing, distribution and profitability.
As digital systems become more integral to operations, the Company is exposed to cybersecurity and data-protection risks that could cause operational disruption, data loss and reputational impact.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Allied Blenders and Distillers Limited manufactures, markets and distributes Indian Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL), with a diversified brand portfolio spanning Mass Premium and Prestige & Above (P&A) price segments across whisky, vodka, rum, gin and brandy. The Company serves state government-owned beverage corporations, the Canteen Stores Department (defence), and private distributors/retailers domestically, reaching consumers through an extensive network of licensed retail outlets, bars, restaurants and hotels, while international markets are served through distributor and partner relationships. ABDL operates an extensive pan-India manufacturing and distribution network combining owned and partner (third-party) facilities, and has been strengthening backward integration into ENA, malt and PET packaging.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's real GDP growth projected in the range of 6.8%-7.2% for FY2026-27, supported by resilient consumption, continued government expenditure and an improving private investment cycle
- Rising disposable incomes and evolving consumer preferences expected to continue supporting premiumisation trends across categories
- Indian spirits industry transitioning from a volume-led to a value-led market, supported by premiumisation across price segments, rising aspirational consumption and growing preference for branded, better-quality offerings, contributing to improved realisations and stronger profitability potential
- Structural long-term demand support from favourable demographics, low per capita consumption, an expanding legal-drinking-age population, rising disposable incomes and increasing global acceptance of Indian spirits
- Premium and super-premium segments continue to outpace broader industry growth, reflecting a structural shift from volume-led to value-led consumption
- Input cost volatility and supply-chain pressures - key inputs such as Extra Neutral Alcohol (ENA), glass, grains and packaging materials remain vulnerable to inflationary trends, agricultural variability and supply disruptions, potentially necessitating calibrated pricing actions
- Regulatory and taxation complexity from the state-level regulatory framework affecting pricing, distribution, licensing and route-to-market execution
- Illicit and unorganised market competition creates pricing distortions and can dilute consumer trust in formal categories
- ABD Maestro: two strategically located manufacturing facilities in the pipeline to support efficient small-batch premium production
- Travel Retail: 4 travel retail locations and presence in 4 countries currently, with more locations in the pipeline

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: ABDL's capex programme is focused on strengthening backward integration, securing critical inputs (ENA, Malt, PET) and expanding manufacturing capabilities, implemented through Phase I and Phase II investments. Phase I (captive integration): (1) a captive PET bottle manufacturing facility at Rangapur, Telangana was commissioned during the year, with ~600+ Mn bottles per annum capacity and ~70-75% internal requirement coverage, and has been EBITDA accretive since Q3 FY26; (2) a single malt distillery at Rangapur, Telangana (~4.0 MLPA capacity) continued under development to secure captive malt for the Prestige & Above portfolio and build Single Malt whisky capability; (3) an ENA capacity expansion at an acquired ~11 MLPA distillery in Aurangabad, Maharashtra (operations commenced February 2025), with a major expansion initiative underway to significantly increase ENA distillation capacity toward a planned 66 MLPA (also referenced as a planned expansion to ~61 MLPA), strengthening backward integration in a key operating market. Phase II (downstream growth), initiated during the year: bottling capacity expansion in Uttar Pradesh (bottling-unit upgradation, ~40 Cr investment) to strengthen manufacturing presence in a key growth market; bottling capacity expansion at the Aurangabad, Maharashtra facility to support western-market and international demand; and an ENA Distillery (Dual Mode) project in Vizianagaram, Andhra Pradesh via an up-to-50% stake acquired in KION Blenders Industries Private Limited. The narrative text also cites additional investment figures of approximately ~260 Cr, ~110 Cr, ~54 Cr and ~300 Cr associated with the ENA/Phase II projects, but the source formatting does not cleanly attribute each figure to a single named project, so they are reported here only as a range of disclosed amounts rather than assigned individually. Collectively, the current projects are expected to enhance EBITDA margins by ~300 bps by FY28 and an incremental ~100 bps by FY29. ABD Maestro (the super-premium to luxury subsidiary) separately has two strategically located manufacturing facilities in the pipeline to enable efficient small-batch premium production.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, forward-looking, disciplined; strong emphasis on premiumization, backward integration, and long-term margin expansion; leadership transition (Amar Sinha) underway with clear 3-year roadmap; cautious on near-term margin pressure but optimistic on H2 recovery

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Strong leadership position in the Indian whisky segment, anchored by flagship Mass Premium brand Officer's Choice Whisky with deep brand recall and consumer franchise
- Three 'millionaire brand' whiskies in Prestige & Above (Officer's Choice Blue, Sterling Reserve B7, ICONiQ White Whisky) providing scale across large, fast-growing price points
- Extensive pan-India manufacturing network combining owned and third-party (exclusive/non-exclusive) facilities, enabling operational flexibility and proximity to consumption centres
- Extensive distribution reach - 80,000+ retail touchpoints domestically and an asset-light, high-margin export model across 36 countries
- Backward integration into ENA, malt and packaging (PET) enhancing supply security, cost structure and margin resilience
- Diversified super-premium to luxury portfolio via ABD Maestro (80%-held subsidiary), built on a 'Build, Buy & Partner' model spanning whisky, gin, vodka and rum

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Geopolitical disruptions (West Asia) impacting input costs & exports; inflationary pressure on distribution & packaging; delayed Telangana price hike; ESOP charges (₹5-6cr/quarter); brand cannibalization risk between ICONiQ and SRB7/OC Blue

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: OC Brandy in AP (12-13M case market) is a hidden millionaire brand opportunity; ₹27/franchise fee elimination in UP will materially boost OC margins; ABD Maestro’s 3-year path: CM3 negative → CM2 neutral → CM3 neutral (EBITDA breakeven by Year 3); CSD approvals are a structural moat for premium brands

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition - UP] Announced Jan-26 acquisition of a non-operational distillery cum bottling facility (land, building, plant, machinery and licences) in Moradabad, UP from National Industrial Corporation Private Limited for Rs 70 Cr, to become the 3rd integrated facility.
- [Acquisition - AP] Announced Mar-26 acquisition of up to a 50% stake in Kion Blenders Industries Private Limited (Rs 300 Cr investment, Rs 90 Cr equity split Rs 45 Cr each with the existing shareholder) to set up the 66 MLPA Vizianagaram dual-mode distillery.
- [Regulation] Management flags the UK FTA as margin-enhancing for the premium and luxury portfolio, and describes the state regulatory landscape as supportive with further momentum expected from the Telangana policy and anticipated price revisions.
- [Receivables] Improving sentiment in Telangana for gradual clearance of outstanding dues; historic Telangana overdues and statutory arrears were the driver of the large negative H1FY25 operating cash flow.
- [Management] Amar Sinha joined as Managing Director in 2026 (ex-Radico Khaitan, Whyte & Mackay India), with a Chief Revenue Officer, Group CMO and Chief Procurement Officer also newly appointed or re-designated effective 1 Aug 2026.
